Getting Started

Source: vignettes/governance.Rmd
governance.Rmd
library( governance )
library( dplyr )

The governance package scores nonprofit governance from the IRS Form 990. Since the 2008 redesign, Part VI of the 990 asks every full filer about its board, its written policies and its disclosure practices, and Parts IV and XII record audits and financial oversight. The package turns those answers into 16 indicators of recommended practice and combines them into a single governance index, gov_score.

The index comes from an item response model fit to every 501(c)(3) organization that e-filed a full Form 990 for tax year 2023 (about 271,000 organizations). Its parameters are fixed, so a score from any year is on the same scale: 0 is the average 2023 filer, and one unit is one standard deviation of governance among 2023 filers.

The workflow has two steps:

  1. get_features() codes the raw 990 fields as binary practice items.
  2. get_scores() scores the items with the 2023 model.

Step 1: Get input data

get_features() expects one row per filing with the raw efile fields from Form 990 Parts IV, VI and XII and Schedule M. The companion panel990 package retrieves them; get_governance_data( years = 2023 ) returns a data frame ready for the next step. See vignette("download-data") for the tables and fields.

The package also ships dat_example, a 5,000-organization sample of raw 2022 fields, so you can try the workflow without downloading anything.

data( "dat_example", package = "governance" )

# a 200-organization subset keeps the examples fast
set.seed( 57 )
rows        <- sample( nrow(dat_example), 200 )
dat_example <- dat_example[ rows, ]

Step 2: Code the practice items

get_features() adds 16 GI_* columns, one per practice, coded 1 when the organization reports the practice, 0 when it does not and NA when the question was left blank. It also adds five RISK_* disclosure indicators and the 12 features used by the older 2018 model.

features <- get_features( dat_example )

# share of organizations reporting each practice
features |>
  summarise( across(starts_with("GI_"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer( everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "share" ) |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
item share
GI_REVIEW_AUDIT 0.50
GI_AUDIT 0.39
GI_AUDIT_CMTE 0.38
GI_ACCRUAL 0.64
GI_INDEP_MAJOR 0.83
GI_MINUTES_BOARD 0.92
GI_MINUTES_CMTE 0.81
GI_990_BOARD 0.69
GI_COI 0.64
GI_COI_DISCLOSE 0.58
GI_COI_MONITOR 0.54
GI_WHISTLE 0.48
GI_RETENTION 0.52
GI_COMP_CEO 0.40
GI_COMP_OTH 0.28
GI_990_WEB 0.10

Step 3: Calculate the scores

get_scores() appends the governance score and its standard error, four specific-factor scores and gov_count, the number of the 16 practices the organization reports.

scores <- get_scores( features )

vars <- c( "ORG_NAME_L1", "gov_score", "gov_score_se", "gov_count" )

scores[ , vars ] |>
  head() |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
ORG_NAME_L1 gov_score gov_score_se gov_count
849 BLUE RIDGE WOMENS CENTER INC 0.85 0.44 12
2532 SPECTRUM THEATRE ENSEMBLE -0.72 0.30 7
2699 WESTERN INSTITUTE FOR VETERANS RESEARCH 1.03 0.51 14
2478 Spida Inc 0.13 0.20 10
531 Oak School of Delray Beach Inc -1.00 0.43 4
3673 GROW WELLNESS FOUNDATION -1.94 0.65 0 
hist( scores$gov_score,
      main = "Governance scores, 200 example organizations",
      xlab = "gov_score (0 = average 2023 filer)" )
